The one-process-per-arm candidate screen passed finite numerical/unit checks but was slower; it was rejected, not promoted to product or added to the final current window.

Final current-window comparison uses ordinary AD Hyle and retained native peer off/on images, three fresh timing processes plus one independent memory observation per arm. Use only the final host review for new numerical summaries; no historical window pooling.
Natural IDs, actual target/draft verification work and native arithmetic can differ across modes/engines; no cross-arm same-token speed or full quality claim is assumed.
